text:
sam: noticed a cluster of OOMs and a P99 spike after yesterday's kernel swap to kern_v7. Rolling average GPU mem free dropped and fragmentation jumped. stack traces show workspace alloc failures on prefill paths.

maria: ugh. which hosts and which model/seq lengths? any flame graphs?

sam: repro on ded-nyc-03, model open-70b-qat, seq distrib skewed: median 256, 95th 2048. quick log snippet: 
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:44Z] oom: workspace_alloc(size=1.18GB) failed, free=224MB, largest_free_block=196MB
[2026-03-18T09:12:44Z] traceback: runtime::prefill_alloc -> kv::reserve -> slab_alloc
```

sam: perf counters before->after (kern_v6 -> kern_v7): 
- kernel exec time per token: 1.6ms -> 1.5ms (good)
- avg occupancy: 82% -> 63% (bad)
- fragmentation estimate: 12% -> 36%
- prefills hitting workspace limit: 0.8% -> 6.3%

kai: so raw kernel perf improved but memory packing worse. my hunch: v7 changed buffer alignment/stripe size and made slabs less space-efficient for mixed-size KV entries.

rachel: any change to our buffer_reuse flag or thin_slab thresholds in the build?

sam: I grepped the patch: added 256-byte alignment for warp-friendly kernels and switched to 4KB mini-pages in allocator; buffer_reuse default still true but reuse path now bails on mismatched alignment -> allocs fall back to fresh slabs.

maria: that explains fragmentation jump. fallback creates mesh of small free slots. we should test two mitigations in parallel: (A) reduce prefill per-request cap, (B) enable thin_slab_coalesce or lower alignment. also consider smaller mini-page (2KB) to reduce internal waste.

kai: agree. quick experiment configs I propose:
```
# experiment A - prefill cap
runtime.prefill.per_request_cap = 128MB
runtime.prefill.global_soft_cap = 12GB

# experiment B - allocator tuning
allocator.mini_page_kB = 2
allocator.alignment = 64
allocator.coalesce_on_free = true
```

sam: ran a short smoke with prefill cap=128MB on ded-nyc-03 for 1h. Results vs control: prefills hitting workspace limit dropped from 6.3% -> 0.9%, P99 latency for seq>1024 dropped ~18%, overall throughput ~-2% (expected). fragmentation stayed ~28% (improved but not fixed).

rachel: wow good win for prefill cap. we should also measure tail under sustained load. Did you capture per-request mem usage histogram?

sam: yes, pasted percentiles: 
```
req_mem_mb: p50=48 p75=96 p90=180 p95=340 p99=740 p999=1250
```

eve: given that distribution, per-request hard cap at 1.5GB is dangerous; a safer per-request soft cap + fallback to streaming decode is preferable. Proposal: 
- soft_prefill_cap_per_request=256MB (allow override)
- if prefill_needed > 256MB -> auto-fallback to streaming prefill/decode path and mark request as "streamed" in traces
- enable thin_slab_coalesce by default for v7 for 48h canary

maria: sounds good. also eviction: we saw small entries that are hot but waste many tiny slots. switch eviction demote policy to size-aware LRU: demote small KV entries first to keep big contiguous free spans. config:
```
kv.eviction.policy = "size_aware_lru"
kv.demote.size_threshold = 8KB
kv.demote.to_tier = "cooled"
```

kai: for metrics, capture: slab_fragmentation_ratio, avg_free_span_size, prefills_blocked, streamed_fallback_ratio, p99_latency_by_seq_bucket. Add regression alert if fragmentation > 30% for 10m.

infra-bot: deploy triggered by sam: canary/allocator-v7-tune -> ded-nyc-03 [started]

sam: running canary with: prefill.soft_cap_per_request=256MB, allocator.mini_page_kB=2, allocator.coalesce_on_free=true, kv.eviction=size_aware_lru. will collect 6h run then decide.

rachel: once canary runs, let's also try a non-invasive patch: enable buffer_reuse_force=true to see if reuse path reclaims more. low risk.

sam: noted. tentative rollback plan if OOMs increase: revert kern_v7 on canary and toggle prefill cap to 64MB cluster-wide.

eve: owners: sam (canary), kai (metrics/alert), maria (eviction policy change + bench), rachel (buffer_reuse probe). checkins in #eng-runtime at +2h, +6h.

maria: I'll run microbench for alignment vs mini-page size later today and share a spreadsheet. initial hypothesis: 64-byte alignment + 2KB mini-pages + coalesce_on_free will reduce fragmentation to <18% without perf regression.

sam: thanks all. I'll post perf traces + flame samples once the canary has 2h of data.

infra-bot: deploy canary/allocator-v7-tune -> ded-nyc-03 [succeeded] (2026-03-18T10:02:21Z)

eve: nice. incremental, measurable approach. if this stabilizes, we'll schedule a staged rollout and update the kernel changelog with allocator compatibility notes.

sam: end of thread for now - will update with numbers.
